- Which tickets can be paid by card or bank is chosen in Events, under "How people can pay".
- Refunds are made in the Stripe or GoCardless dashboard. The hub shows them by itself.

## Who to ask
- The church's treasurer or money team.
- A master admin, if you cannot open the page.
pages.peep:
# My evacuation plan

If you would need help to get out of the building in a fire, a short plan here means the people on duty know what to do. The plan is yours. You can change it or delete it whenever you like.

## Who can use it
- Anyone in the church's address book can make their own plan.
- A master admin can also enter a plan for someone else, with that person's agreement.
- If you are not in the address book, the page asks you to talk to the church office.
- Building compliance has to be switched on for the church. If it is off, the page says so.

## Make your plan
1. Under **What help would you need to get out quickly?**, say what help you need. For example, "I cannot use stairs."
2. If you like, fill in **Who helps?**, **Where do they go?** and **Any equipment?**
3. Tick the box to agree that the people on duty may see the plan.
4. Press **Make the plan**.

## Change your plan
1. Open the page. Your plan is already filled in.
2. Change what you need to.
3. Press **Save the plan**.

## Check your plan once a year
1. Each plan has a date to review it by. You see it under the buttons.
2. When that date has passed, a note asks you to check the plan is still right.
3. Check it and press **Save the plan** again. This sets the next date a year on.

## Delete your plan
1. Press **Delete the plan (no longer needed)**.
2. Say yes to the question. The plan is gone.

## Enter a plan for someone else (master admins)
1. Under **Whose plan?**, choose the person. **My own** goes back to yours.
2. Fill in the plan with them, and tick to say they have agreed.
3. Press **Make the plan** or **Save the plan**.
4. The plan then says it was entered by you with their agreement.

## Good to know
- Please do not put medical details in the plan.
- Only you and master admins can open your plan here.
- When you are in the building, the fire wardens and the duty stewards on duty for that building see it on the fire roll-call. Nobody else sees it.
- It is never sent by email.
- Every change, and every delete, is kept in a log.
- Until the hub goes live, plans cannot be made here, because the hub is not yet private. Tell a steward or the church office in person instead.
- Under-18s are not offered in the **Whose plan?** list.

## Who to ask
- The church office, if you are not in the address book or need help with your plan.
- A master admin, if you would like them to enter a plan for you.
pages.permissions:
# Permissions

This is where master admins choose who may do what in the hub, section by section. Master admins can always do everything. Here you tick who else may.

## Who can use it
- Only master admins can open it.
- Anyone else is told they cannot open the page.

## Find a permission
1. Type in the search box, for example "upload" or a person's name.
2. Under **By section**, each section is a card, such as **Events & rooms**, **Communications** or **Money**. Press a section's name to open or close it.
3. Each card says how many actions it has, and how many exceptions.

## Choose who may do something
1. Open the section and find the action.
2. **Master admins** is always ticked. You cannot change that.
3. Tick who else may. The groups of ticks are:
   - **Core teams covering**: the core teams that look after a job's teams.
   - **Everyone on these jobs' teams**: everyone on the teams that do that job.
   - **Their admins**: the admins of those teams.
   - **Leaders of the teams ticked here**: the leaders of the teams you tick for this action.
   - **Choose teams…**: press it to tick single teams.
4. A bar appears at the bottom. Press **Save** to keep your changes, or **Cancel** to undo them.

## Give one person an exception
1. Under the action, find **Exceptions: these people too** and press **+ Add a person**.
2. In **Person**, pick someone from the address book.
3. Choose **Until (optional)** if it should end on a date.
4. Fill in **Why (master admins see this)** so others know the reason.
5. Press **Add**. It is saved straight away.

## Remove an exception
1. Press **Remove** beside the person, either under the action or in **Exceptions**.
2. Say yes. It is taken away straight away.

## See all exceptions
1. Press **Exceptions**. The number shows how many there are.
2. Each row shows the person, what they may do, why, who added it and when it ends.
3. An exception ending within a week is marked "ends in ... days".

## See what has changed
1. Press **History**.
2. It lists the last 100 changes: when, what changed, and who did it.

## Good to know
- Changes reach people the next time a page opens.
- An exception can only add a permission. It never takes one away.
- Some actions are marked "Set in code today: moves here later". They are shown so you know who can do them, but cannot be changed here yet.
- **Safeguarding** and **Pastoral care** are not set here. Use the link on each card to go to [Safeguarding settings](safeguarding-settings.html) or [Teams & groups](teams-admin.html).
- Every change, exception added and exception removed goes into the history.
- If an action has no ticks, only master admins (and any exceptions) may do it.

## Who to ask
- Another master admin.
- The church office, if you are not sure who should be allowed something.
pages.picture-library:
# Picture library

This page holds pictures the church uses again and again, such as a club's or a regular service's picture. Events can use a picture from here, so every date and every copy shows the same one.

## Who can use it
- The church office, the bookings admins and master admins.
- Anyone else is told "This page is for the church office, the bookings admins and master admins."
- The picture library has to be switched on for the church. If it is off, the page says so.

## Add a picture
1. Under **Add a picture**, press **Choose a picture** and pick one.
2. The **Name** fills in from the file name. Change it to something clear.
3. Add **Tags** if you like, with commas between them.
4. Press **Add to the library**.

## Use a picture in an event
1. Open the event in What's On.
2. Press **Choose from library** and pick the picture.

## Rename a picture or change its tags
1. Find the picture on this page.
2. Change its **Name** or **Tags**.
3. Press **Save**.

## Replace a picture
1. Find the picture and press **Replace**.
2. Choose the new picture.
3. Every event using it now shows the new picture. The page says how many.

## Delete a picture
1. Find the picture and press **Delete**.
2. The page tells you how many events use it.
3. Press **Delete** again to be sure, or **Cancel**.
4. Events that used it show no picture until someone picks another.

## Good to know
- Each picture says how many events use it, or "Not used by any event".
- Replacing is better than deleting when you just want a fresh picture.

## Who to ask
- The church office.
- A master admin, if the library is switched off or you can't open the page.
pages.places-admin:
# Places

This is where the church's buildings, rooms, kit and outside venues are set up, with who approves bookings, how members' bookings work, and the prices for hiring rooms. Everything else in the hub uses these, so renaming is always safe.

## Who can use it
- The church office, the bookings admins and master admins can open it.
- Anyone else is told "This page is for the church office, the bookings admins and master admins."
- Master admins also see a **Church details** button, for the church's name, enquiry email and logo.

## Add a building
1. Open **Sites**. Type the **Name**, **Postcode** and **Address**.
2. Press **Check** to make sure the postcode can be found. It still saves if not.
3. Press **Add site**.
4. For a new church, **Seed the starting rooms** makes one site with a set of starting rooms. Rename them as you like. It will not run twice.

## Add a room
1. Open **Rooms**. Type the **Name**.
2. Choose **Kind**: **A room at a site** or **Online (a video room)**.
3. Choose the **Site**, how many it holds under **Capacity**, and a **Colour** for the calendar.
4. Tick **Step-free access**, **Members may book** and **Outside hirers may book** as they apply.
5. Press **Add room**.

## Fill in a room's profile
1. **Fill in your rooms** lists what each room still needs. Press **Fill in**, or **Profile** on the room.
2. Add **Photos**. The first is the main picture; use **Make main** to change it.
3. Fill in the size, floor, nearest toilets and kitchen, and how many it holds for each layout.
4. Give a **Fire-safety maximum**. No booking can ever be for more people than this.
5. Tick its **Facilities**, and write a **Short description** and **House rules for this room**.
6. Under **Members' bookings**, choose whether members' bookings are confirmed straight away or wait for approval.
7. Press **Save the profile**.

## A room made of other rooms
1. In a room's profile, under **Made up of other rooms**, tick its parts (at most four). An example is a hall with a folding wall.
2. Booking the whole room then takes every part, and booking any part makes the whole unavailable.

## Kit, catering and outside venues
1. **Kit**: type the **Name**, where it **Lives in**, and **How many**, or tick **Unlimited**. Press **Add kit**. You can set a hire price and tick **Can be moved to another room**.
2. **Catering**: add things people can ask for with a room, with a price **Per person** or **Per item** and the **Notice needed (working days)**. Press **Add to the menu**. Each item asked for with a booking goes on its quote: the number asked for times the price. The office checks the quote before approving and invoicing.
3. **Outside venues**: search by name or place, or fill in the boxes by hand, and press **Save venue**.

## Who approves bookings
1. Open **Who approves**. Each building is listed.
2. Choose the **Safeguarding lead** and **Safeguarding deputy**.
3. Under **Bookings admins**, choose a person and press **Add**. Press the cross to take someone off.
4. Core Team can always approve a booking, whatever is set here.

## Booking settings for each building
1. Open **Bookings**.
2. Choose whether members' bookings are confirmed straight away or wait for the office.
3. Fill in **Send booking requests and cancellations to**. Use an office address, not a person's own.
4. Tick **Email the day's setup sheet to that address each morning** if you want it.
5. Set the minutes after which a booking not marked arrived is flagged. 0 turns it off.
6. Set the opening hours used for the room use report.
7. Under **Services on the rota keep rooms busy**, press **Add a service**, fill in **What**, **From**, **To**, the days and the rooms, then **Save the services**.

## Hire prices
1. Open **Hire prices**. Under **Kinds of booking**, type a name and press **Add a kind of booking**.
2. Tick **For the public** to put it on the public booking form, and **Charged** if it is priced. Choose a **Members' rate** if members pay less.
3. Under **Terms and conditions**, choose the kind, write the terms and press **Save as a new version**.
4. Under **A room's prices**, choose the **Room** and **Kind of booking**, fill in the prices, and press **Save these prices**.

## Good to know
- **Take out of use** hides a building, room or piece of kit without deleting it. **Bring back** undoes it.
- A building or room still needed by bookings to come stays in use, and you are told why.
- Floor plans can only be put up once the church goes live on the hub.
- Hirers who accepted older terms keep the version they accepted.

## Who to ask
- A master admin, if you cannot open the page or need Church details changed.
- The church office, about prices and who approves bookings.
pages.planner:
# Rota Planner

This is where the Sunday rota is built. You add the services for a term, put people in each slot, check who said they are free, and send everyone their rota by email.

## Who can use it
- Team leaders and team admins of the teams that serve on Sundays can open it. So can master admins.
- If you run one team, you see and change only your own team's slots. A line such as "2 more handled by another team" tells you other slots are there.
- Master admins see every slot.
- Anyone else is turned away.

## Add the services for a term
1. Choose the term in the **Term** box: **Spring** (January to April), **Summer** (May to August) or **Autumn** (September to December).
2. Press **Populate**. The hub adds the church's main service on every Sunday of that term, this year.
3. Press **Add Practices** to add a weekly Thursday evening practice (7:30 to 9:30pm) for every week of the term.

## Add one service
1. Press **+ Service**.
2. Choose the **Date** (it starts on next Sunday) and **What kind**.
3. Press **Add**. Nothing is saved if you press **Cancel** or the cross.

## Change a service
Each service is a row. Changes save as you make them.
1. Change the date, the team's start and end times, or the kind of service.
2. Type anything for the team in **Notes...**.
3. Type the service leader and the speaker in their boxes. Names come up from the address book, or type a guest's name.
4. Choose a video call room, or **No video call**. **Join** opens the call.
5. Tick the teams that are needed. Ticking the children's team adds its usual slots.
6. If the church shows Sundays in What's On: tick **In What's On**, type the public title, the time it **Starts**, and **A line for the public (optional)**.

## Put people on the rota
1. Press the round button with the box on it, on the right of the row. It shows **Available**, **Declined** and **Pending** (not answered yet).
2. Drag a name from **Available** into a slot.
3. Drag a name from one slot to another to move them.
4. Press the small **×** on a name to take them off.
5. Use **+ Role** to add another slot, such as a second singer. Point at a slot's name and press its **×** to remove the slot.
- A name in gold means that person has not said if they are free that day.
- A green dot on a row means every main slot is filled.
- **Sundays served this month** shows how often each person is on.

## Fill the rota for you
1. Press **Auto-Populate** and say yes.
2. It fills empty slots on the main Sunday services with people who said they are free. It keeps to each person's limit per month.
3. It only fills slots for your own team.
4. It also copies each Sunday's team onto the practice in the days before it. **Sync** on a practice row does this for one practice.

## Ask people when they are free
1. Press **Gather Avail**.
2. Type the term you want, as shown in the list, and press OK.
3. Say yes. Everyone on the teams for that term gets an email with a link to the [availability form](index.html).

## Say your team's part is done
1. On the term heading, press the button with your team's name and "not done".
2. It changes to a tick. Press it again to undo.
3. If anyone changes your team's slots later, the tick goes and you need to press it again.
- "waiting" means another team has not finished yet.

## Send everyone their rota
1. Type your email in **Sending as**. Replies come to you.
2. Choose a term in **Send term**, or leave **All active terms**.
3. Press **Send all rotas** and say yes.
4. Each person gets an email with their dates, PDFs of their own rota, their household's rota, a wall planner and the full rota, and calendar files.
- It will not send until every team has ticked its part as done. It tells you who is still to finish.

## Send or print one person's rota
1. Choose the person in the name box.
2. **Indiv** makes a PDF of their rota. **Home** makes one for their household. **Wall** makes a wall planner.
3. **Send** emails that person their rota.
4. **Full PDF** prints the whole rota. **Excel** saves it as a spreadsheet.

## Finish a term
1. Press **Archive** on the term heading and say yes. Its services leave the list.
2. Archived terms are listed at the bottom. Press **Restore** to bring one back.

## On a phone
- The top bar has the term, **+ Service** and **More**. **More** holds every other button.
- Tap a service to open it.

## Good to know
- Past dates are hidden. Press **Show past dates** to see them. This is remembered on this device.
- **Hide Assigned** hides people who are already on that day's rota from the lists.
- The bin on a row deletes that service for good. It cannot be undone.
- Removing a slot also takes off whoever was in it.
- The service leader and speaker are the same ones the [Preaching plan](preaching-plan.html) shows.
- The **?** button opens the step-by-step guide.

## Who to ask
- Your team leader.
- A master admin, if you cannot open the page or see the wrong slots.
pages.prayer:
# Prayer

This page is for prayer requests at any time, and for praise reports: how prayers have been answered. Your requests are private.

## Who can use it
- Anyone signed in can ask for prayer, see their own requests, and read and share praise reports.
- The pastoral team also see a **Requests to pray for** tab with every request.
- If the church has a prayer team, it sees a **Prayer team** tab with the requests people chose to share with it.
- The pastoral team, the prayer team, and the person leading the coming Sunday's service may see a **For Sunday** tab.
- Master admins also see **The prayer team** box, to name the church's prayer team.
- If the church does not use prayer requests, the page says so.

## Ask for prayer
1. Open the **Prayer request** tab.
2. Write what you would like prayer for. Or press **Speak** and say it.
3. Under **Who may see it**, choose **The pastoral team only**, or the pastoral team and the prayer team (if the church has one).
4. Under **Happy for this to be prayed for in the Sunday service?** choose **No**, **Yes, with my name** or **Yes, without my name**. It is No unless you choose yes.
5. Press **Send my request**.
6. To ask for something more, press **Ask for something else**.

## See and change your requests
1. Open the **My requests** tab.
2. Each request shows when you sent it and who can see it.
3. To change your mind about Sunday, use **In the Sunday service?** under the request.
4. To take a request away, press **Take it back** and say yes. The pastoral team will no longer see it.

## Say a prayer has been answered
1. In **My requests**, find the request.
2. Under **Has it been answered? Say how**, write what happened if you like.
3. Tick **Share the answer with the church, to encourage others** if you want to. Leave **with my name** ticked, or untick it to share without your name.
4. Press **It has been answered**. It now shows **Answered**.

## Share a praise report
1. Open the **Praise reports** tab. You see what others have shared.
2. Under **Share an answer to prayer**, write it, or press **Speak** and say it.
3. Leave **with my name** ticked, or untick it.
4. Press **Share it**.

## Pray for others (pastoral team and prayer team)
1. Open **Requests to pray for** (pastoral team) or **Prayer team** (prayer team).
2. Each request shows who asked, when, and whether it may be prayed for on Sunday.
3. These are private. Please do not pass them on.
4. The pastoral team can press **Hide it** on a praise report to take it off the list.

## The Sunday list
1. Open **For Sunday**.
2. It lists the requests people are happy to have prayed for in the Sunday service, from the last four weeks, that are not yet answered.
3. A name shows only where the person asked for it. Otherwise it says **No name given**.
4. Press **Print** to print the list.

## Name the prayer team (master admins)
1. At the foot of the page, in **The prayer team**, type the name of the team or group exactly as it is in the address book.
2. Press **Save**. Leave it empty if the church has no prayer team.

## Good to know
- Your name goes with your request, so you can be prayed for by name.
- Nobody else sees a request, apart from the pastoral team and, if you choose, the prayer team.
- A request is never read out on Sunday unless you said yes.
- **Take it back** removes the request. It cannot be undone.
- Before the church goes live on the new hub, nothing can be sent from this page. The button says when requests open. Until then, speak to a church leader in person.
- If the church has not yet named who receives requests, the page says messages cannot be sent from here yet.
- If someone is in immediate danger, call 999.

## Who to ask
- The pastoral team, or a church leader in person.
- A master admin, if you cannot send a request or the prayer team is not shown.
pages.preaching-plan:
# Preaching plan

One table of the coming services: what each one is, who is preaching, who is leading, and who is reading what.

## Who can use it
- The Pastor, the church's leaders and master admins can change it.
- People who plan the rotas can read it but not change it.
- Anyone else is told "For the preaching team and the rota planners".
- The preaching plan has to be switched on for the church. If it is off, the page says "The church does not use the preaching plan."

## Read the plan
1. Each row is one service, for the next three months.
2. The columns are **Date**, **Description**, **Speaker**, **Service leader** and **Readers**.
3. Tick **Show past services** to see the ones already gone.
4. Where a sermon has been planned, a **Sermon plan** link under the speaker opens it.

## Change a service
1. Type in **Description**. This is what What's On shows for the service.
2. Type the **Speaker** and **Service leader**. Names come up from the address book. You can type a guest's name too.
3. Move to another box. It saves by itself and says "Saved".

## Add readers
1. Press **+ Add a reader**.
2. Type the name in **Reader** and the Bible passage in **Passage**, for example John 3:1-17.
3. Press **×** to take a reader off.

## Choose the Pastor (master admins)
1. Master admins see a card called **The Pastor** at the top.
2. Press **Choose the Pastor in Team emails** to pick them there.
3. The Pastor can then change this plan without being an admin.

## Good to know
- There is no Save button. Each box saves when you leave it.
- If a box says "That did not save", try again.
- These are the same details as the [Rota Planner](Planner.html), What's On and the app. Change one here and they all change.
- The list shows the church's kinds of service, and anything ticked to show in What's On.

## Who to ask
- The Pastor or the church's leaders.
- A master admin, if you cannot open the page or the Pastor needs changing.
pages.present:
# Present

This page shows a group session's slides, Bible verses, pictures and quiz. A leader presents from their phone or laptop. Everyone else follows on their own phone. The TV view shows the slides full screen on the TV.

## Who can use it
- A group's leaders can present its sessions. Master admins can too.
- The group's team can open a session and follow along, but cannot present.
- Anyone else is told the session belongs to a group they are not part of.

## Find a session
1. Open **Present** from the Menu.
2. You see your groups' sessions, the next ones first.
3. Press **Open** on the one you want.
4. If there are none, plan one in the session planner with slides, verses or pictures to show.

## Present a session
1. Open the session and press **Present**.
2. Everyone following sees the first slide straight away.
3. You see the slide everyone sees, **Up next**, **Your notes** and a timer.
4. Press **Next slide** to move on, or the back arrow to go back. You can also tap any small slide picture to jump to it.
5. Arrow keys, Space, Page Down or a clicker also work on a laptop.

## Show it on the TV
1. On the computer connected to the TV, open the session, then press **Open TV view** (bottom left). Leaders see this button.
2. A new window shows the slides full screen, with nothing else on it.
3. Present from your phone or laptop as usual. The TV follows you.
4. If it says to click for sound, click once on the TV screen.

## Blank the screen
1. Press **Blank the screen** (or the B key) when you want people's attention.
2. Press **Show the slide again** to bring it back.

## Play a video in the slides
1. On a slide with a video, press **Play**. It plays in step on every screen.
2. Press **Pause** or **Start again** as you need.
3. Sound is off on phones. Press **Sound off here** to turn it on for your screen.
4. If the video is only a link, press **Open the video**.

## Hand over or stop
1. Another leader can press **Take over presenting**. You see who has it.
2. When you are done, press **Stop presenting**.

## Follow on your phone
1. Open the session. If nobody is presenting yet, it says so and waits.
2. When the leader presents, your phone shows their slide and moves with them.
3. Press **Browse on my own** to look back through the slides.
4. Press **Back to presenter** to catch up again.

## Run a quiz
1. When you reach a quiz in the session, choose how to play.
2. **Play in teams**: no phones. Name the teams (**+ Add a team** if you need more), tick the bonus point if you like, then **Start: question 1**. Tap each team that got it right, then **Show the answer on the TV** and **Next question**.
3. **Play on phones**: a code and a QR code show on the TV. People join on their phones with a nickname. Press **Start: question 1**, then **Show the answer now**, **Show the leaderboard** and **Next question**.
4. To remove a rude name, tap it under **Who's playing**, then **Remove**.
5. Press **End the quiz and delete everything** when you finish.

## Good to know
- The whole session is fetched when it opens, so slides change at once even on weak Wi-Fi.
- If the Wi-Fi drops, a screen keeps its slide and catches up when it is back.
- If a session has nothing to show yet, add slides, verses or a picture to it in the session planner.
- **How to present** opens a two-minute guide.
- Phone quiz nicknames, answers and scores are deleted when you end the quiz. A quiz nobody ends is deleted about a day after it started.

## Who to ask
- The group's leader, if you cannot see a session.
- A master admin, if you should be a leader of the group but are not.
pages.privacy:
# What we hold about someone

This page finds everything the church's hub holds about one person. Use it when someone asks to see their data, or to check before deleting someone. It searches everything on the [information asset register](data-records.html).

## Who can use it
- The church's data protection leads and master admins can use it.
- Anyone else is told it is for the data protection leads and master admins. If you want to know what the church holds about you, ask the church office and they will pass it on.
- Data protection leads are chosen by the church office on [Data records](data-records.html), under **Who keeps these**.

## See what we hold about someone
1. Under **Who**, start typing a name and pick it from the list. Or type their email address.
2. If this is for a data request, pick it under **For a data request**. This is optional. Only open requests are listed.
3. Press **See what we hold**.
4. You see their name, their email addresses, whether they have ever signed in to the hub, and how many records were found.
5. Below that is one box for each kind of data on the register. Each says why the church holds it, the lawful basis, how many records there are, and what those records hold.

## Download the export
1. After a search, press **Download the export**.
2. A file downloads with every record shown on the page.
3. If you picked a data request, the download is logged against that request.
4. Check the file before you send it. Remove anything that is about someone else.

## Print a summary
1. After a search, press **Print this summary**.
2. The search box and buttons are left off the printout.

## Good to know
- Care, pastoral and safeguarding records are counted but never shown here. They say "Held, and not shown here" and who to ask. Ask that person to provide those records. They are left out of the export too.
- If a name is not in the address book, the page says so. Pick from the list, or type their email address instead.
- "Nothing on the register names this person" means no records were found.
- Record the request itself, and its deadline, on [Data records](data-records.html), under **Data requests**.

## Who to ask
- The church's data protection lead.
- A master admin, if you cannot open the page.
pages.quiz:
# Join the quiz

This is the page people use to play a quiz on their own phone. The leader shows a code on the TV, and each person joins with a nickname.

## Who can use it
- Anyone in the room with the code. No account and nothing to sign.

## Join
1. Scan the QR code on the TV, or go to the web address it shows.
2. Type **The code on the screen**, if it is not already filled in.
3. Type **Your first name or a nickname**.
4. Press **Join**. You see "You're in!".

## Answer a question
1. The question and four answers show on your phone, with a countdown.
2. Tap your answer. On a computer you can press A to D, or 1 to 4.
3. You get one answer per question. Then look up at the screen.

## See how you did
1. When the leader shows the answer, your phone says if you were right, and your points.
2. A quick right answer scores more.
3. Your place and score show, then the top five on the leaderboard.

## Good to know
- Your nickname, answers and score are deleted when the leader ends the quiz. If nobody ends it, they are deleted about a day after it started.
- If the leader removes your name, you are asked to join again with another name.
- When the quiz ends, press **Join another quiz** to play again.

## Who to ask
- The leader running the quiz.
pages.retention:
# Due for deletion

This page lists form answers whose time is up. Each form says how long its answers are kept. Nothing is deleted until you confirm it here.

## Who can use it
- Only master admins can use it, because only they can delete records.
- Other admins who open it are told the list is for master admins.

## Delete answers that are due
1. Look under **Due now**. Each answer shows who sent it, the form, who it was for, and the dates.
2. Every answer is ticked. Untick any you want to keep for now.
3. Press **Delete the ticked answers**.
4. Say yes to the question. The answers go, with their medical details and any files sent with them.

## See what is coming up
1. Look under **Due in the next 30 days**.
2. These cannot be deleted yet. They move to **Due now** when their day comes.

## Check the forms against the register
1. Look under **What the register says**. It lists how long each kind of record is kept.
2. If a form keeps its answers longer than the register says, a yellow note names it.
3. Change that form, or change the register in **Data records**.
4. If the register is not started yet, start it in **Data records**.

## Good to know
- Look at this page once a month.
- Answers with medical details are marked.
- A deleted answer cannot be brought back.
- What was deleted, and who did it, is kept in a log.
- Incidents and concerns are never on this list. They are kept.

## Who to ask
- A master admin.
- Whoever looks after data protection for the church.
pages.risk:
# Live risk register

This page shows how the church manages, day to day, the risks in its professional health, safety and fire risk assessments. It adds to those assessments. It does not replace them, and the trustees remain responsible for the building's safety.

## Who can use it
- The office, the trustees and master admins can open it. The page names who does the office and trustees jobs.
- The office keeps it: hazards, reports and the plan for visitors who need help.
- The trustees read it and sign off snapshots.
- Building compliance has to be switched on for the church. If it is off, the page says so.
- Until the church goes live on the hub, the page is read only and nothing is saved. Keep your paper record for now.

## Choose a building and a view
1. If there is more than one building, press its name at the top.
2. Choose a view: **Hazards**, **Professional assessments**, **Changes since**, **Snapshots** or **Visitors who need help (GEEP)**.

## Check the hazards
1. Open **Hazards**. The dials and **The building's own assessments** are at the top.
2. Each hazard has a colour. It comes from the building's checks that control it.
3. Press a hazard to see its **Controls (the checks)** and its **Issues**, open or resolved.

## Add hazards (office)
1. Press **Add the starter hazards** to add a ready-made list. Each comes with this building's checks as its controls.
2. Or press **+ Add a hazard**. Fill in **What could go wrong**, **Who could be hurt**, **Likelihood** and **Severity**, and press **Add it**.

## Change or close a hazard (office)
1. Press the hazard.
2. Under **Change it**, set **Likelihood** and **Severity**, choose its **Controls**, and add **Notes**.
3. Press **Save**. Or press **Close the hazard**.

## Put up a professional report (office)
1. Open **Professional assessments**.
2. Under **Put up a report**, choose **Which**: fire, or health and safety.
3. Fill in **Done on**, **Next review** and **The assessor**. Add **The report (PDF)** if you have it.
4. Press **Put it up**. The review check is recorded, and due again on the next review date.

## See what has changed
1. Open **Changes since**.
2. It lists hazards and checks added or changed since the last professional report.
3. Tell your assessor about these at the next review.

## Sign off a snapshot (trustees)
1. Open **Snapshots**.
2. Under **Sign off and keep a snapshot**, add a **Note** if you like.
3. Press **Sign off and keep a snapshot**. A dated copy is kept with your name.
4. Press **Open** on an old one to read it, or **Print or save as PDF**.

## The plan for visitors who need help (office)
1. Open **Visitors who need help (GEEP)**.
2. Fill in how you find out who needs help, where they wait, who helps them, and any equipment.
3. Press **Save the GEEP**. It is due for review a year later.

## Good to know
- The building's own health and safety and fire assessments are linked under **The building's own assessments**, with a **Print** link.
- Their findings that are still Medium or High are listed, with the checks that watch them.
- The duty team see the visitors plan on the fire roll-call.
- Safeguarding has its own register. Trustees see a link to it.

## Who to ask
- The church office.
- The trustees, about snapshots and sign-off.
pages.room:
# A room's page

This page shows one room: its photos, size, how many people it holds, its facilities and when it is free over the next seven days. The church website links to it for each room that can be hired.

## Who can use it
- Anyone can open it, with no need to sign in. They only see rooms that are for hire.
- Church members who come from Book a room see a members' version. It shows any room, for hire or not, and also lists the room's kit.
- The floor plan shows only to the people the room's setting allows: everyone, members and the office, or the office only.
- If a room cannot be found, or is not for hire, the page says so and points back to all the rooms.

## Look at the room
1. Click a small photo to see it large.
2. **The room** gives its floor area, size, ceiling height, where to find it, step-free access and the nearest toilets and kitchen, where these are filled in.
3. **How many it holds** gives the number for each way it can be set out, and the most allowed for fire safety.
4. **Facilities** lists what the room has, and says if you may bring your own caterers.
5. **House rules** shows any rules for the room.

## Ask to book it
1. Look at **When it is free** for the next seven days.
2. Click a free time. The booking form opens with the room, date and time filled in.
3. Or press **Ask to book this room** to open the booking form for this room.
4. On the members' version the button is **Book a room** instead, and takes you to the members' booking page.

## Ask a question
1. If the church has an email address set up, it is shown next to the button.
2. Click it to email the church about this room.

## Good to know
- Only what has been filled in for the room is shown. A blank item is left out.
- On the members' version, **Kit** shows what is in the room and what can be brought in.

## Who to ask
- The church office, about hiring a room or anything on this page.
- Whoever looks after the rooms, if a detail or photo is wrong.
pages.rooms:
# Book a room

This page shows when the church's rooms are free, and lets you book one for a band practice, a meeting or anything else. It also lists your own bookings, so you can cancel them or say you have arrived.

## Who can use it
- Team leaders, the core teams, the church office and the bookings admins can open it.
- A bookings admin who is not one of the others only sees the rooms at the buildings they look after.
- Anyone else is told it is for team leaders and core teams, and to ask their team leader.
- Only rooms that members are allowed to book are shown.

## See when rooms are free
1. Press **Day** to see every room on one day, or **Week** to see one room for seven days.
2. Pick the date in the **Day** (or **Week from**) box, or use the arrows to go earlier or later.
3. In week view, choose the room in the **Room** box. If the church has more than one building, choose it in the **Site** box.
4. Your own bookings are marked. A room that is closed that day is not shown, or shows as closed.
5. Press **Compare rooms** to see two or more rooms side by side.

## Book a room
1. Click a free time on the calendar, or press **Book a room**.
2. If there is a **What kind of booking** box, choose one. Church or ministry use is free. A kind marked "(charged)" is priced.
3. Tick the room under **Room** or **Rooms**. Tick more than one if your event needs several rooms.
4. Fill in **Date**, **Start** and **Finish**.
5. Choose **Time to set up first** and **Time to clear away after** if you need them. The room is held for that time too.
6. Fill in **What is it for?** and **How many people**. Choose **Set out as** if you want the room laid out a certain way.
7. Tick **We need sound or projection**, refreshments or kit if you need them, and say what.
8. Read the messages under the form. They say if the room is free, and whether it is confirmed straight away or waits for the office.
9. Press **Book it**, or **Ask for it** if it has to wait for the office. Then press **Done**.

## Book the same time every week
1. In the booking form, choose **Repeats**: **Every week**, **Every two weeks** or **Every month, on the same weekday**.
2. Choose **Until**, the last date.
3. The dates are listed, each marked free or not. Dates that are not free are left out. Untick any you do not want.
4. Press **Book it** or **Ask for it**.

## Cancel a booking
1. Find it under **Your bookings**.
2. Press **Cancel**. For a repeating booking you can also press **Cancel this and the ... after it**.
3. Say yes to the question. The room is free again and you are emailed.

## Say you have arrived
1. On the day of a confirmed booking, press **We've arrived** under **Your bookings**.
2. It then says you are marked as arrived.

## Good to know
- You can book up to 100 bookings at once (rooms times dates).
- A charged booking always waits for the office to confirm the price. You see a price for it, at the members' rate if there is one.
- If a room can never hold the number of people you give, it says so and will not book.
- When a booking is confirmed you are emailed the details and a calendar file. When it waits, you are emailed again once the office decides.
- If a booking overlaps one the office made, you cannot cancel it here. Ask the office.
- If someone books the same time just before you, it tells you to look again.
- Bookings admins see a link to **Room bookings**, where they can approve, move or cancel any booking.

## Who to ask
- The church office, about prices, approvals or a booking you cannot cancel.
- Your team leader, if you cannot open the page.
pages.rota-reports:
# Rota reports

This page shows who serves, how often, and where the gaps are on the rotas. It only reads the rotas as they are saved. It changes nothing.

## Who can use it
- Master admins see every rota team.
- Leaders of a rota team see only the teams they lead.
- A leader who leads no team with a rota is told there is nothing to show.
- Rota reports have to be switched on for the church. If they are off, the page says so.
- Anyone else is told "This page is for master admins and the leaders of rota teams."

## Choose the dates and team
1. Set **From** and **To**. To start with, it shows three months back to three months ahead.
2. If you can see more than one team, pick one under **Team**, or leave it on all teams.
3. Practices are left out unless you tick **Include practices**.

## Find unfilled slots
1. Press **Unfilled slots**. This is where the page opens.
2. You see each empty slot, with its date, service, slot and team.

## See an overview of each service
1. Press **Overview**.
2. Each service shows its date, time, how many slots are filled, and which are still empty.

## Find clashes
1. Press **Clashes**.
2. You see anyone who is down for two places at once on the same day, and why.

## See how often people serve
1. Press **How often people serve**.
2. Each person shows how many services and slots they served, on which teams, and when they last served.

## See one person's serving
1. Press **One person's serving**.
2. Pick them under **Who**.
3. You see every time they are on the rota in these dates.

## Find people not on the rota
1. Press **Not on the rota**.
2. You see people on a rota team who were not on the rota at all in these dates.

## Download a report
1. Open the report you want.
2. Press **Download (CSV)**. It opens in a spreadsheet.
3. The button only shows when the report has something in it.

## Good to know
- This page shows serving only. It does not show who came to church.
- To fill a gap, use the rota planner, not this page.

## Who to ask
- Your team leader.
- A master admin, if you cannot open the page or reports are switched off.
pages.safeguarding-risk:
# Safeguarding risks

This is the church's safeguarding risk register. It holds the standing risks of each activity, how they are controlled, and who looks after them. It holds risks, controls and dates only: never a child, a family or a concern.

## Who can use it
- The safeguarding lead and deputy keep the register for their own site.
- The trustees and master admins can read it, take snapshots and record review items. They see "Read only".
- A leader of a group that is in the register sees that group's risks only, read only.
- Anyone else is told who the page is for.
- Safeguarding, and the register, must be switched on for the church in Church settings.

## Move around the register
1. If the church has more than one site, choose it under **Site**.
2. Use the tabs: **Dashboard**, **Standing risks**, **Event assessments**, **Warnings**, **Annual review** and **Snapshots**.

## Read the dashboard
1. Open **Dashboard**. It shows dials for leaders' checks, sessions with enough leaders, consent forms, event assessments and incident follow-ups.
2. It also lists what is still needed for this year's annual review.
3. Press **Work them out now** to bring the numbers up to date.

## Add an activity
1. Open **Standing risks**.
2. Under **Add an activity**, press one of the church's own groups to add it.
3. Or choose the **Kind**, type a **Name**, and press **Add it**.

## Add or change a risk
1. On an activity, press **Add a risk**, or **Edit** on a risk already there.
2. Fill in **What could happen** and **Who could be harmed**.
3. Choose **How likely** and **How bad**, from 1 to 5.
4. Tick any **Controls the hub watches**, and write **Other controls, in words**.
5. Choose how likely and how bad it is after the controls.
6. Add an **Owner** and a **Review by** date.
7. Add anything **Still to do**, with who and by when.
8. Press **Save**. Tick **Closed** to close a risk. It is kept, not deleted.

## Use the starter list
1. On an activity, press **Add from the starter list**.
2. Untick any you do not want. Ones already added are marked.
3. Press **Add the ticked ones**, then change each one to fit how your church runs it.

## Link an incident to an activity
1. On **Standing risks**, **Incidents to link to an activity** lists this year's incidents. Only the date and the event show.
2. Choose the activity, and press **Link**. That activity's risks are then marked to look at again.

## Check the warnings
1. Open **Warnings**. Each one says **Act now** or **Soon**, and what to do.
2. The safeguarding lead can press **Go to it** to fix it.
3. Press **Refresh now** to work them out again.

## Event assessments
1. Open **Event assessments**. It lists coming events at this site that need a safeguarding sign-off, and where each has got.
2. The lead presses **Open the event's assessment** to write or sign it.
3. Press **Read it** to read one. A trustee can say the trustees have noted it.

## The annual review
1. Open **Annual review**. Each item says who records it.
2. Press **Record it**, add a note if you like, and press **Record it** again.

## Take a dated snapshot (trustees)
1. Open **Snapshots** and press **Take a snapshot**.
2. Add a note if you like, and press **Take it**.
3. Press **Open it** to read an old one, or **Print** it.

## Good to know
- Use general words only. Never name a child, a family or a concern.
- **Print / save as PDF** on **Standing risks** prints the whole register.
- A risk past its review date shows **Review overdue**.
- Warnings are counts only. Names stay on the pages that fix them.

## Who to ask
- The church's safeguarding lead or deputy.
- A master admin, if the register is switched off.
pages.safeguarding-settings:
# Safeguarding settings

This page sets who looks after safeguarding, and the periods and rules that every new form and event starts with. It also holds the settings for the safeguarding risk register.

## Who can use it
- Admins and the safeguarding lead or deputy can open it.
- Only admins can change who the safeguarding lead and deputy are. The lead sees the name, and "An admin changes who it is."
- Anyone else is told "These are set by admins and the safeguarding lead."

## Name the safeguarding lead and deputy (admins)
1. Under **Who looks after safeguarding**, choose the **Safeguarding lead** and the **Deputy** for each building.
2. If there is more than one building, pick the one whose lead the forms reach first.
3. Add **The lead's phone number (optional)**. It shows beside "call 999" on the "I'm worried" form.
4. Press **Save the settings**.
- Only adults are offered. The lead and the deputy must be two different people.
- Until a lead is named, concerns, requests for care and prayer requests cannot be sent.

## Set how long form answers last
1. Under **Forms**, find each kind of form.
2. Choose **Answer lasts**: one event, the end of the term, the end of the school year, or a number of days or months.
3. Choose **Kept after that**: how long it is kept before it is due for deletion.
4. Press **Save the settings**.

## Set the leader rules
1. Under **Leaders**, fill in **One leader for every … children** and **… and for every … under-8s**.
2. Choose how long **A DBS check counts for** and **Safeguarding training counts for**.
3. Tick **Every leader must have an in-date DBS check and training** if you want that for every event.
4. Press **Save the settings**.

## Set up the safeguarding risk register
1. Under **Safeguarding risk register**, type which team are the trustees. If Church settings already says who does the trustees job, it is changed there instead.
2. Set what **"Due soon" means**, in weeks.
3. Set when each dial on the register turns green or amber.
4. Set how many **AI-drafted assessments a day** the church and each person may have.
5. Tick which signed assessments **The trustees note**, such as camps, overnights or anything overseas.
6. Press **Save the settings**.

## Name your lead and your guidance
1. In **What your church calls its safeguarding lead**, type your own name for the role, such as "Parish safeguarding officer". Leave it empty to keep "safeguarding lead".
2. In **The safeguarding guidance your church follows**, type its name and its web address. It shows on every event assessment.
3. Press **Save the settings**.

## Add your church's own questions
1. Under **Your church's own required questions for event assessments**, press **Add a question** and type it.
2. Press **Remove** to take one away.
3. Press **Save the settings**. They are asked on every event assessment, as well as the fixed checklist.

## Apply the settings to forms and events already made
1. Save the settings first.
2. Under **Forms and events already made**, the page counts the forms and events that differ.
3. Press **Also apply to … forms** or **Also apply to … events**, and say yes.
- Answers already given keep their dates. Events with no leaders yet take the new settings on their own.

## Good to know
- New forms and new events take these settings from now on. An event can still change its own.
- **References and declarations count for** sets how long a reference and the confidential declaration last.
- **Flag public liability cover under** marks an event amber if its insurance is lower. It is £1 million unless you change it.
- **Look at a group's risks again** sets how much a group can grow or shrink before its risks are looked at again.
- The trustees never see a child, a concern or anyone's medical details on the register.
- Fire wardens and duty stewards are now set in Health and safety settings.

## Who to ask
- The church's safeguarding lead.
- An admin, to change who the lead or deputy is.
pages.safeguarding:
# Safeguarding

This is where the church keeps each event safe: who is leading, whether there are enough leaders, their DBS checks and training, incidents and accidents, and concerns. Anyone signed in can report a concern from here.

## Who can use it
- Anyone signed in can open the page and press **Report a concern**.
- The front page shows events coming up in the next month. Admins see all of them. Leaders see the events they lead. The safeguarding lead and deputy see their own site's events.
- An event's own page is for its leaders, admins and the safeguarding lead. Anyone else is told so, and can still report a concern.
- Only the safeguarding lead and deputy see the concerns reported to them.
- The safeguarding lead, deputy and admins also see buttons for **Safeguarding settings** and the **Safeguarding risk register**. Master admins see **Due for deletion**.

## Report a concern
1. Press **Report a concern**.
2. If you are not on an event, choose **Where**.
3. Fill in **Who it is about (if you know)**, and **What you saw, heard or were told, in the words used, and when**.
4. Press **Send to the safeguarding lead**.
5. It goes to the safeguarding lead only. You cannot read it back, so say everything now.
- If a child or adult is in danger right now, call 999.

## Read and note concerns (safeguarding lead and deputy)
1. Open the page. **Concerns reported to you** lists each one, marked **New** or **Seen**.
2. Press **Mark seen and add notes**, write **What you have done**, and press **Save**.
3. Press **Notes** later to add more.

## Open an event
1. Under **Coming up**, find the event and press **Open**.
2. The top shows the event, with **Check-in** (for admins and leaders) and **Report a concern**.

## Add leaders and helpers
1. On the **Leaders** card, press **Add**.
2. Type a name under **Find by name**, then press **Leader** or **Helper**.
3. Or press **From the rota**, tick the people on the rota that day, and press **Add the ticked people**.
4. Press the cross next to a name to take them off.
- Only people who have signed in can be found with **Add**.

## Check there are enough leaders
1. The tiles show **Children booked**, **Under 8**, **Leaders** and **Leaders needed**.
2. A green bar says there are enough. An amber bar says how many more are needed.
3. A child whose consent form has not come in is counted, but not as under 8.

## Set the event's ratios and rules
1. On the **Leaders** card, fill in **One leader for every … children** and **… and for every … under-8s**.
2. Set how many years a DBS check and training count for.
3. Tick **Works with under-18s** for a kids club or youth event. Then every leader and helper must have an in-date DBS check and training.
4. Or tick **Every leader must have an in-date DBS check and training**.
5. Press **Save**.

## Record a leader's checks (safeguarding lead)
1. Next to a leader, press **Checks**.
2. Choose the **DBS check** status and the **Level of the DBS check**.
3. Fill in the dates: DBS seen, training, a church leader's reference, and the confidential declaration.
4. Press **Save**. Never record the DBS certificate number, or a copy of it.

## Someone not cleared yet
1. On an under-18s event, a person without in-date checks is marked **not cleared yet**, or is not added.
2. Bring their checks up to date, then press **Check again**.
3. Or the safeguarding lead can press **Exception**, give **The reason**, and press **Record the exception**. It is kept with their name.

## Share medical details with the leaders
1. Some families say their consent form is still correct. Their medical details came from an earlier event.
2. The safeguarding lead sees **Medical details to share with the leaders**. Press **Share with this event's leaders**.

## Record an incident or accident
1. On **Incidents and accidents**, press **Record one**.
2. Fill in **When**, **Who was involved** and **What happened**.
3. Say whether first aid was given, and by whom, and whether a parent or carer was told.
4. Press **Save**.
5. The safeguarding lead can press **Follow-up** to say what was done afterwards, and **Download** to save the list.

## The safeguarding assessment
Trips, overnights, holiday clubs and off-site events that work with under-18s need one. Bookings open only once it is signed off.
1. Choose a template under **Start from a template** and press **Start the assessment**. Or describe the event and press **Draft it** for a first draft by AI. Check every line of it.
2. If the host sent their own requirements, add the file, their web pages or the words, and press **Read the requirements**. Check the questions, then press **Confirm these as required questions**.
3. Answer every question on the checklist, or tick **Not applicable** and say why.
4. Check each risk: how likely, how bad, and what you do about it. Press **Add a risk** for more, and **Add something still to do** for open jobs.
5. Press **Save**, then **Ready for sign-off**.
6. The safeguarding lead or deputy presses **Sign it off**. Bookings then open.
- **Print / save as PDF** gives a copy to keep.
- The safeguarding lead or a master admin can open **Not needed for this event?** and press **It isn't needed**, with a reason.

## Good to know
- Use general words only. Never name a child, a family or a medical detail in an assessment.
- Changing a signed assessment sends it back for sign-off, and bookings close until then.
- **DBS checks and training running out** lists the next six weeks, and any already run out.
- If you help with under-18s, **Your checks** shows your own dates.
- Someone whose check has run out cannot be added to anything that works with under-18s.

## Who to ask
- The church's safeguarding lead or deputy.
- The church office, if no safeguarding lead is set for your site.
pages.sermons-admin:
# Sermons

This page looks after the church's sermons. Sermons come in by themselves from the church's podcast on Spotify, and here you add the series, Bible passage and speaker, hide any you don't want shown, or upload one by hand. The live service and videos are on [Watch](watch-admin.html).

## Who can use it

- Master admins can always use this page.
- Anyone else can use it only if a master admin has added them under **Who can look after sermons**.
- Everyone else sees "Only the people named can look after sermons".
- Only master admins see the **Who can look after sermons** part and can add or remove people.
- The same people also look after the [Watch](watch-admin.html) page.

## Connect the podcast

Do this once. After that, new episodes come in by themselves.

1. Find the podcast's RSS address. In Spotify for Creators it is under Settings, as the RSS feed.
2. On this page, go to the podcast card and paste it into **The podcast's RSS address**. It must start with https://.
3. Press **Save the address**.

The podcast is read every hour, so new episodes appear within the hour. The card tells you what the last read found: when it was, how many episodes, and how many were new. If the last read did not work, it says why. Check the address.

To stop new episodes coming in, clear the address and press **Save the address**.

## Add the series and passage to a podcast sermon

Podcast sermons are marked **From Spotify**. A sermon with neither a series nor a book shows **add its series or passage**.

1. In the **Sermons** list, press **Add series and passage** on the sermon.
2. Choose or type the **Speaker**. Names used before are suggested.
3. Choose the **Series**, or **Not part of a series**.
4. Choose the **Bible book** and type the **Passage** (for example 1:1-11).
5. Tick or untick **Show it in the app**.
6. Press **Save**, or **Cancel** to leave it.

The title, words and recording come from Spotify and can't be changed here. What you add is kept when the podcast is read again.

## Show or hide a sermon

- Press **Hide** on a sermon to take it out of the app. It shows **Hidden**.
- Press **Show** to put it back. It shows **Shown**.
- A hidden podcast sermon stays hidden when the podcast is read again.

## Upload a sermon by hand

This is the backup way, for a sermon that is not on the podcast.

1. Press **+ Upload a sermon by hand (if one is not on the podcast)**.
2. In **The recording**, choose the audio file. An MP3 is best. It can be up to 300 MB.
3. Type the **Title**.
4. Fill in **Speaker** and **Date** (it starts at last Sunday), and the **Series**, **Bible book** and **Passage** if you like.
5. Add **Notes (optional)**.
6. Leave **Show it in the app** ticked to show it straight away.
7. Press **Upload**. A bar shows how far the upload has got.

Uploaded sermons are marked **Uploaded here**. To change one, press **Change**. You can choose **New audio (only if it needs replacing)**, edit the details, and press **Save**.

If the upload fails, the sermon is kept but hidden and marked **Needs its audio**. Press **Add its audio** to try again.

## Add a series

1. Under **Series**, press **+ Add a series**.
2. Type the **Name**.
3. Add **A line about it (optional)**.
4. Choose **A square picture (optional, JPEG or PNG)** if you have one.
5. Press **Add the series**.

Each series shows how many sermons are in it, and whether it has a picture.

## Who can look after sermons (master admins)

1. In **Add someone**, start typing a name and choose the person from the list.
2. Press **Add**.
3. To take someone off, press **Remove** next to their name.

## Good to know

- Sermons are never deleted here. Hide them instead.
- Series can't be deleted, renamed or given a new picture on this page once added.
- Nothing you do here changes anything on Spotify.
- Podcast sermons play from Spotify's own recordings.
- A new podcast episode arrives already shown in the app.
- If an uploaded recording's length can't be read, it is saved but not shown. Try again with an MP3.
- Shown sermons appear on [Watch & Listen](watch.html).

## Who to ask

- For podcast or sermon questions: whoever looks after sermons.
- To be added to the people who look after sermons: the church office, who can ask a master admin.
pages.services-settings:
# Your services

This page sets the kinds of service and meeting your rota offers, and the people a service names, such as who leads it and who preaches. Each service keeps its own rota, plan and building.

## Who can use it
- The church office and master admins can open it and change everything on it.
- Anyone else is told they cannot open the page.
- It is also the "Your services" step when a new church is being set up.

## Add a kind of service or meeting
1. Under **Kinds of service and meeting**, type a name in the box, such as "10am Parish Eucharist".
2. Press **Add**.
3. Or press one of the ideas under the box, such as **+ Morning Prayer**.
4. Press **Save** at the foot of the page.

## Set up a service
1. On its card, check the name.
2. Tick **A service** if it should show on What's on, the preaching plan and the planners. Leave it unticked for a meeting or practice.
3. Fill in **Team arrives** and **Ends**. For a service, also fill in **Starts (public)**.
4. If the church has more than one building, choose the **Usual building**.
5. Under **The teams it needs**, tick the teams this service needs.
6. Under **Rota places it starts with**, type the rota places, with a comma between each.
7. Press **Save**.

## Change the order
1. Press **↑** on a card to move it up.
2. The order here is the order the rota offers them.
3. The first service is the one "Populate term" fills each Sunday.
4. Press **Save**.

## Add a role a service names
1. Under **The roles a service names**, type a role, such as "Intercessor".
2. Press **Add**, or press one of the ideas, such as **+ Preacher**.
3. Leave **On the slides** ticked if the role should go on the team slides. Untick it if not.
4. Press **Save**.

## Remove a service or role
1. Press **Remove** on its card.
2. Press **Save** to keep the change.

## Good to know
- Nothing is kept until you press **Save**. If you leave the page first, your changes are lost.
- When saved, it says "Saved. New services on the rota use these from now on."
- If something needs fixing, the page lists it in red next to **Save**.
- Roles are people typed on each service, not rota places.
- If nothing has been saved yet, the page shows starting lists for you to change.

## Who to ask
- The church office.
- A master admin, if you cannot open the page.
pages.session-planner:
# Session planner

This page is where groups such as the children's or youth groups plan their sessions, week by week. The preaching team can also plan sermons here. Each plan can hold what to show on screen, so it can be presented from the Present page.

## Who can use it
- A group's leaders can add and change every plan of their group. Master admins can too.
- The group's team can read the plans, but not change them.
- Master admins also set up the groups, under **⚙ Groups**.
- Anyone else is asked to speak to a master admin about being added to a group.
- If the church does not use the session planner, the page says so.

## See the term
1. Tap your group's name at the top.
2. **The term** lists each plan by date, with who is on and who is away.
3. Tap a week to open its plan.
4. Press **Print the term** for a paper copy.

## Plan a week
1. Press **+ Add a** and the day (for example **+ Add a Sunday**). The next date is filled in.
2. Fill in the **Lesson title**. Choose a **Programme**, a **Lesson code** and a **Link to the lesson** if you use them.
3. Under **This week**, choose **A special week (say what)** or **No session this week** if it is not a normal week.
4. Press **Choose a passage** to add the Bible passage.
5. Press **Save**.

## Who is on and who is away
1. Press **Fill in from the rota**. It fills in who is on from the rota and who is away from the availability form.
2. To add someone by hand, pick them in **Add someone** and choose **as on** or **as away**.
3. Press the cross by a name to take them off.

## Build the session
1. Use **+ Add a part** to add a part, such as a game, story or prayer.
2. Tap a part to open it. Fill in the **Title**, **Minutes**, **Leader's notes**, **Things to bring** and any links.
3. Press **Upload a file** to add a worksheet, picture or video to the part. Save the plan first.
4. Drag the ⠿ handle to put the parts in order.
5. Press **Remove this part** to take one out.
- Everything people need to bring shows together under **Things to bring**.

## Add things to show on screen
1. In an open part, choose from **+ Show something**.
2. Pick **Bible verses**, **Memory verse**, **Picture**, **Video file**, **YouTube**, **Song**, **Timer**, **Text slide**, **Quiz**, **PowerPoint** or **Open a link**.
3. Fill in the small form and press **Add it**.
4. For a picture or video, upload it to the part first.
5. For a quiz, type each question, then its four answers with the right one first. Leave a blank line between questions.
6. Drag the steps to put them in order. Press the cross to remove one.

## Choose a Bible passage
1. Choose where it comes from: **Free Bibles**, **API.Bible** or **Bible Gateway**.
2. Choose the **Version** and type the **Passage**, for example John 3:16-21.
3. Press **Show it**, then **Import into the plan**. With Bible Gateway, the plan keeps only the reference and a link.

## Plan a sermon (preaching team)
1. Press **+ Plan a sermon for a service** and pick the service.
2. The date, speaker and readers come from the Preaching plan. Change those there, not here.
3. Add the **Sermon title**, **Series**, passage and the outline, then **Save**.

## Share, print or present
1. Press **Email the plan**. It goes to every leader of the group and this week's team.
2. Press **Print** for a paper copy.
3. Press **Present** to show the plan's slides, verses and pictures.
4. Press **Delete this plan** to remove it. This cannot be undone.

## Set up a group (master admins)
1. Press **⚙ Groups**.
2. Fill in the card under **+ A new group**: name, kind, ages, where and which day it meets, and the team.
3. Add leaders with **Add a leader**. They can edit every plan and get every plan by email.
4. Add any programmes and the usual parts of a session.
5. Press **Add the group**. Use **Save** or **Remove the group** on an existing one.

## Good to know
- If you leave without saving, the page asks first.
- The page says who last changed a plan, and when.
- PowerPoint slides can be added once the church goes live on the new hub.
- A YouTube video may show an advert. An uploaded video never does.
- Removing a group keeps its plans, but nobody can open them from here.

## Who to ask
- The group's leader, about a plan.
- A master admin, to be added to a group or to set one up.
pages.setup:
# Setting up your hub

This page is the list of steps a new church works through to set up its hub. Each step opens the page that does it, and you can come back here at any time.

## Who can use it
- Only master admins can open it.
- Anyone else is told they cannot open the page.

## Work through the steps
1. Open the page. The bar at the top shows how far you have got, and the line under the title says how many steps are done.
2. Press **Start** on a step. It opens the page that does that step.
3. Do the step on that page. A bar along the foot of the page says which step you are on.
4. Press **Next** in that bar to go to the next step, or **All the steps** to come back here.
5. A step that is done shows a tick, and its button says **Change**.

## The steps
1. **Your church**: its name, logo, address and words, its giving details and the e-news.
2. **Your buildings**: each building and its rooms, and who looks after its safety.
3. **Your teams**: the teams and groups people belong to, and which jobs each one does.
4. **Your services**: the kinds of service and meeting, and the roles a service names.
5. **Your people**: the address book. Everyone the hub knows, and the teams they are on.
6. **Who gets told**: who reads requests for care, pastoral concerns and prayer requests.
7. **Safeguarding**: the safeguarding lead and deputy, how long checks last, and the ratios.
8. **Data protection**: your data protection lead, and the record of what the church holds.
9. **Pastoral visitors** (if you want it): the trained people who record pastoral visits.

## Good to know
- You cannot tick a step yourself. A step shows as done once the hub sees it has been done on its own page.
- **Your church** is done once it has a name, an address and an enquiry email.
- **Your buildings** is done once there is a building, a room in it, and a health and safety lead.
- **Your teams** is done once there is a team and someone has chosen who does each job.
- **Pastoral visitors** is optional. It is not counted in the steps done.
- A step marked **Coming soon** cannot be done yet.
- When every step is done, the page says Church HQ will take you through going live.

## Who to ask
- Church HQ, about setting up and going live.
- Another master admin of your church.
pages.signup:
# Event

This page shows one church event, with all its details. Where booking is open, you sign up for it here.

## Who can use it
- Anyone can open a public event, signed in or not.
- Some events are only for attenders, church members or a team. Others are told "That event could not be found, or it is not open to you."
- If you are signed in, your sign-up is linked to your record, and your name and email are filled in for you.

## See the event
1. Open the event from What's on, or from a link you were sent.
2. You see when and where it is, who is organising it, and the write-up.
3. Where booking is open, it says how many places are left, or **Full — waiting list open**.
4. Press the picture to see it whole.

## Sign up
1. Under **Sign up**, fill in **Your name** and **Your email**. **Phone** is optional.
2. If there is more than one ticket, choose the **Ticket**.
3. Under **Who is coming**, type each person's name. Press **Add someone else** for more people, or the cross to remove one.
4. Answer any questions. A star (*) means you must answer it.
5. Add a donation if the event asks for one. It is optional.
6. Use **Anything we should know?** for anything else.
7. Press **Sign up**.
8. You see **You are signed up**, and a confirmation email is on its way.

## Sign up again quickly
1. If you have signed up before, press **Same as last time** to fill in the same people and answers.
2. If the hub knows your household, tick who is coming under **Who is coming from your household?**.
3. Check anything marked **From last time**. If health answers were filled in, tick the box to say you have checked them.
4. On a shared device, press **Not you? Clear** to forget the names.

## Join the waiting list
1. If the event is full, the form says **Join the waiting list**.
2. Fill it in the same way and press **Join the waiting list**.
3. You get an email, and another if a place comes free.

## A series of dates
1. Some events sign you up to every date in a series at once. The page lists the dates.
2. Press **Sign up to all … dates**.
3. If any date is already full, you go on its waiting list.

## Pay for your place
1. If there is something to pay, the page shows how much before you sign up.
2. After signing up, press **Pay by card** or **Pay by bank** where the church takes payment online. You pay on a secure page, and the money goes straight to the church.
3. Otherwise you pay at the door on the day.

## Share the event or add it to your calendar
1. Press **Add to calendar** to put it in your own calendar.
2. Press **Share on WhatsApp** to send it to someone.
3. Public events also have **Facebook**, **X** and **Email** buttons.

## Good to know
- Keep the link you get after signing up. It lets you see or cancel your place, even if the email has not come.
- If someone takes the last place while you are filling in the form, the page says so. Reload it to join the waiting list.
- If the event is cancelled, or bookings are closed, there is no sign-up form.
- **Bookings open after safeguarding sign-off** means the event is waiting to be checked. Please come back soon.
- Until the church goes live on the new hub, health questions are not asked here. Please tell the organiser directly.
- If you were sent an invitation, your name and email are filled in for you.

## Who to ask
- The organiser named on the event.
- The church office, if you think you should see an event and cannot.
pages.sundayserviceplanner:
# Sunday Service Planner

This is where the worship leader plans a Sunday service: the songs, the keys, the order of service and notes for the team. You can then email the plan to everyone on that service.

## Who can use it
- Leaders and admins of the worship (music) team can open it. So can master admins.
- Anyone else is turned away.

## Choose the service
1. At the top, pick the date from the list of coming services. Use **◀** and **▶** to move between them, or **Pick another date**.
2. Choose the service in **Select Service...**. The main Sunday service is chosen for you.
3. **Leader** shows the worship leader from the rota.
4. If a plan was saved for that service, it opens. If not, you get a starting order of songs, **Welcome and Notices** and **Message**.

## Fill in the top
1. **General Notes**: anything the whole team needs to know.
2. **Opening Remarks / Call to Worship**: this goes at the start of the team email.
3. **Key Roles**: the service leader, worship leader, speaker and reader (or the church's own roles). They come from the rota where possible. Type any name to change one.

## Plan the songs
1. Type in **Song title**. Pick the song from the list that comes up.
2. If it is **Not in library**, use **SongSelect** or **YouTube** to find it, or **Upload Song** to add it.
3. Choose up to three keys in **Key 1**, **Key 2** and **Key 3**. The files for each key show, with **Open File**.
4. **Available** and **Missing** show which keys have chord sheets.
5. Type in **Notes for the band...**.
6. The small number by a song is how many Sundays it has been used. A dark number means its highest ever, so you may want to rest it.
- If the leader has played the song before, their last key and note are filled in for you.

## Change the order
1. **+ Add Song** adds a song. **+ Add Item** adds anything else, such as a reading or prayers.
2. Drag the dots (**⠿**) to move a song or item.
3. Press **▶** or **▼** to open or close a song.
4. Press **×** to remove it.
5. **songs database viewer** opens the song library.

## Notes for each person
1. **Service Team & Roles** lists who is on the rota for that service.
2. Type anything for one person in **Role Specific Notes**.
3. **Closing Remarks / Blessing** goes at the end of the team email.

## Save the plan
1. Press **Save Schedule**.
2. It says "Service saved."

## Email the plan
1. Press **Email Team**. This saves the plan first.
2. In **Your Email (reply-to)**, type your email. Replies come to you.
3. Press **Email Whole Team**. It goes to everyone on the service and the church's leadership team.
4. Or choose a name under **Or email one person:** and press **Email This Person**.
5. It says "Sent" when it has gone.

## Good to know
- Nothing is saved until you press **Save Schedule** or **Email Team**. If you leave first, your changes are lost.
- The email has a link to a simple song list, with the songs, CCLI numbers and notes.
- People the plan is for can see it on Home in the app.
- The projection software picks up the plan and the key roles.
- If a plan was emailed but never saved, the emailed order opens.
- The **?** button opens the step-by-step guide.

## Who to ask
- The worship team leader.
- A master admin, if you cannot open the page.
pages.team-mail:
# Team emails

This page sets up how a team can send emails as itself. The email says it is from the team, and replies go to the team's own address, or to the sender if the team has none.

## Who can use it
- Master admins only.
- Team emails have to be switched on for the church. If they are off, the page says so.
- Anyone else is told "This page is for master admins."

## Choose the Pastor and the office admin
1. In **The Pastor and the office admin**, pick a person under **Pastor** and under **Office admin**.
2. Press **Save**.
3. They may send as any team except a safeguarding team.

## Set up a team
1. Find the team's box under **Teams**.
2. Type the team's **Shared email address**, if it has one. This is optional.
3. Under **Leads** and **Deputies**, pick people from **Add someone…**. Press **×** next to a name to take them off.
4. Tick **Safeguarding** if it is a safeguarding team.
5. Press **Save** on that team's box.

## Clear a team's settings
1. Press **Clear these settings** on the team's box, and say yes.
2. Nobody can send as that team until it is set up again.

## Good to know
- Team emails open when the hub goes live. Until then, a note says so, nothing can be saved, and nobody can send as a team.
- A team's leads and deputies can send as it. So can the Pastor and the office admin, unless it is a safeguarding team.
- A safeguarding team can only be sent as by its own leads and deputies: not the Pastor, the office admin or a master admin. The hub keeps only the outline of each email: when, who, and the subject.
- Emails still leave from the hub's one sending address. The team's mailbox gets a copy.
- Teams come from [Teams & groups](teams-admin.html). Add, rename or archive a team there, and it shows here.

## Who to ask
- A master admin.
pages.teams-admin:
# Teams & groups

This is the one list of every team and group the church has. The Home choices, "View the site as", the address book ticks and the events pages all use it. It also says which team does each job in the hub.

## Who can use it
- The church office and master admins can open it, add teams, and change names, colours, order and archiving.
- Only master admins can change who does each job, what a group runs, pin boards and core teams. The church office sees these but cannot change them.
- Anyone else is told they cannot open the page.

## Add a team or group
1. Under **Add a team or group**, type its name.
2. Tick **A group, not a rota team** if it is a group without a rota.
3. Press **Add**.
4. Choose the name carefully. It cannot be changed later, but its label can.

## Change a team's label or colour
1. Find the team under **The list**.
2. Type a new label in its name box. It saves when you leave the box.
3. Press the colour square to choose a new colour.
4. **Saved** shows when it has saved.

## Change the order
1. Use the up and down arrows next to a team.
2. The new order saves straight away.

## Rota or group
1. Tick **Has a rota** for a rota team.
2. Untick it for a group without a rota.

## Archive a team, or bring it back
1. Tick **Archived** on the team. It goes from choices around the hub.
2. To bring it back, tick **Show archived**, find the team, and untick **Archived**.

## Choose who does each job (master admins)
1. Under **Who does each job**, each job says what it means, and which teams do it.
2. To add a team, choose it from **Add a team…** next to the job.
3. To take a team off, press the **×** on its name.
4. A job can be done by several teams, or by nobody.

## What a group runs, pin boards and core teams (master admins)
1. **Runs**: tick **Today**, **People**, **Bookings** or **Send** for the parts of the hub this team runs.
2. **Pin board**: choose **None**, the team's own board, or a board shared with other teams.
3. **Core team for**: tick the teams this one leads. Being on this team then counts as being on each ticked team.

## Good to know
- Changes save as you make them. There is no Save button.
- Teams are never deleted. Archiving hides a team from choices but never takes it off anybody, so nothing is lost.
